 Volvo Recalls Nearly 10,000 EX30 Vehicles Over Head Restraint Defect That Could Increase Injury Risk
 Daniel Webster 2026년 10월 19일 월 오후 6:00 UTC 0 Volvo is recalling approximately 9,930 EX30 and EX30CC vehicles because a head restraint cushion may detach during a crash. Affected owners can receive a free repair at an authorized dealership. The Global Guy/Shutterstock Volvo Car USA is recalling nearly 10,000 electric vehicles because a head restraint cushion could detach during a crash, potentially increasing the risk of injury to occupants.
 According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) , the recall affects approximately 9,930 vehicles, including certain 2025–2026 Volvo EX30 models and 2026 Volvo EX30CC models.
 The recall was reported to federal regulators on October 9, 2026, under NHTSA campaign number 26V671000.
 What Is Wrong With the Head Restraints?
 The safety concern involves a cushion attached to the vehicle’s head restraint assembly. According to NHTSA’s recall information, the cushion may detach during a collision, increasing the possibility of injury to vehicle occupants.
 Head restraints are an important vehicle safety feature designed to help limit rearward head movement and reduce the risk of neck injuries in certain crashes.
 A cushion that becomes detached during an accident could compromise the intended protection provided by the head restraint assembly.
 The recall applies to specific vehicles within the affected model years, rather than every EX30 or EX30CC manufactured during that period.
 Which Volvo Vehicles Are Affected?
 The recall covers certain vehicles in the following model years:
 2025 Volvo EX30 
 2026 Volvo EX30 
 2026 Volvo EX30CC 
 Volvo estimates that approximately 9,930 vehicles may be affected by the issue.
 However, owners should verify their individual vehicle’s recall status using its 17-character Vehicle Identification Number (VIN).
 According to the recall announcement, affected VINs became searchable through NHTSA’s database on October 9, 2026.
 Volvo Will Provide Free Repairs
 Volvo dealers will address the problem by applying an adhesive designed to reinforce the head restraint cushion’s attachment.
 The repair will be provided free of charge to owners of affected vehicles.
 Owners should contact an authorized Volvo dealership to confirm whether their vehicle is included and determine when the remedy can be performed.
 Volvo expects to mail official owner notification letters beginning November 30, 2026.
 Advertisement
 The manufacturer’s internal reference number for the recall is R10396 .
 How to Check Whether Your Volvo Is Recalled
 Owners don’t need to wait for a notification letter to check whether their vehicle is included in the recall.
 Visit NHTSA.gov/recalls and enter the vehicle’s VIN to search for applicable safety recalls.
 The VIN can typically be found on the driver’s side of the dashboard near the windshield, on the driver’s door jamb, or in vehicle registration documents.
 Owners can also contact Volvo Car customer service at 1-800-458-1552 and reference recall number R10396.
 If the vehicle is affected, ask the dealership about scheduling the free repair and whether any additional precautions are recommended before the work is completed.
 Why Owners Should Address This Recall Promptly
 Although the defect involves a relatively small component, properly functioning head restraints are an important part of occupant protection.
 A detached cushion during a collision could increase the risk of injury, making it important for affected owners to arrange the manufacturer’s remedy.
 Federal safety recalls generally require manufacturers to provide the specified repair without charging eligible vehicle owners.
 For additional information, visit the NHTSA recall database or contact Volvo directly.
 Vehicle owners should verify their specific VIN and follow the manufacturer’s latest repair instructions, as recall information and remedy availability may be updated.
